## C-99: when the pool finder's +0x1bc is written — the danger map at DoTurn, the planning at the AI turn's start, nothing inside a pass — READ (0x46cdd0, 0x717460, 0x6096c0, 0x792c90, 0x7921a0, 0x790890, 0x47ffb0), unported

WRONG IN PART: +0x1bc has the second writer 0x2715a0, run at every search's start; the rule in force is the section 'C-99: every pool search sets out on its own formation's value, a queue run walks its first search's path'.

The start Movement of a move order (the section above) changes only where a
full-Movement search runs, and those run at four places:

- THE DANGER MAP: the player's DoTurn tail (0x4e4560 at 0x4e4aa4 ->
  0x46cdd0 -> 0x717460), one reach a seen fighting unit of each player at
  war, in player order then the unit list's; +0x1bc is left at the last
  one's GetMaxMoves. Its only other caller is the load (0x47ffb0 at
  0x480d6f).
- THE PLANNING: aiTurnJobs (0x6096c0) puts the planning job 0x791b20 in its
  first group (0x6099a2); 0x792c90 plans the units serially on the one
  finder (pool count 1) walking its array forward (0x792d05 / 0x792d0a,
  0x68 a unit), the order AI_Planning.csv logs; +0x1bc is left at the last
  unit's GetMaxMoves. 0x7921a0 pushes the same job once, at the player's AI
  creation (0x469790, flag +0x98); 0x790890 at the load (0x480d7e).
- No other reach or planning sets it: the homeland's, the tactical pass's
  and the trees' searches (Explore, Move Unit, the reaches without the full
  flag) only read it. Inside a player's pass after its planning the start
  is one value.
- The recorded walks against it (runs/h1_duely1124, city-state 4, its last
  planned unit each turn a 2-Movement one — t91 the Pikeman, t93 the
  Trebuchet, t94 the Man-At-Arms 1310728): t91 after the planning the Heavy
  Chariot 983040's 15:10 -> 16:10 fits a start of 2; t94 after the
  planning its 17:7 -> 18:8 does not (a start of 2 makes 17:7's next node
  18:6 a later turn's). The moves before the turn's first
  UnitOperationSegmentComplete (t91 the Catapult 917507, the Warrior
  851972 and the Catapult 786437; t93 and t94 the Heavy Chariot) are the
  units' carried operations run as the turn activates, before the planning:
  they would set out on the danger map's last unit (t94 a 2, t93 a 3 or 4,
  t91 the Warrior's 1 or 4).
- Open: the t94 run after the planning (17:7 -> 18:8) against the planning's
  last unit; the danger map's last seen unit at DoTurn (the engines' sight
  at that moment against the game's); the carried operations at the turn's
  activation, which the engines do not keep across turns.

## C-98: a boost on an item at or past its cost completes it; a minor's parked progress and project conversion in the replay — READ (0x4cc950 at 0x4cca70..0x4ccab3), both twins

(`perTurnWorld`'s `seatPair`, cpu/harness/replay.ts) and the minors'

## C-108: the trade graph's paths — READ, both twins

- THE GRAPH (Trade_Graph.cpp, the trade manager's +0x110): a vertex per
  city ({player, type 2, city id}); one DIRECTED edge per pair (the node map
  +0x140 keyed by the first vertex, its edge set by the second: 0x540ee0,
  0x5419a0), holding the path last laid from the first to the second
  (+0x338 m_vMostRecentPath, origin first) and whether a route runs on it
  (+0x218 m_bHasActiveRoute: set by AddTradeRoute 0x53e650, cleared by
  0x543100, which keeps the path). `GameState.tradeEdges` /
  `trade_edge_*`, keyed by `tradeVertices` / `_trade_vertices` (a capture
  mints a new city id, so a captured city's edges stop resolving).
- WHO LAYS A PATH: (1) the player's DoTurn (0x4e4560 at 0x4e46ee, after the
  governors' clocks and before the cities) runs 0x4d8a40: each living unit
  with MakeTradeRoute on no active route standing in a city of its owner
  (0x556380) updates the graph from that city (0x5457c0 -> 0x545020): over
  every player's cities but the origin, the edge origin -> city with no
  active route takes a fresh search for the origin's owner (0x5590d0, inline
  or as "Trade Graph Update" jobs 0x541770; set by 0x53e510); a search that
  fails LEAVES the edge's old path (`tradeGraphTurn` / `_trade_graph_turn`,
  `refreshTradeEdges`). (2) A route's start (0x555380): the edge origin ->
  destination's path where it holds one (0x553010), else 0x5526a0's, laid
  on the edge (AddPath 0x53eb50 -> 0x53e900); then AddTradeRoute
  (`commitRoute` / `_trade_store_course`, `setTradeEdge`).
- WHO READS IT: CanStartRoute's path 0x552ed0: the edge origin -> destination
  holds a path, else a fresh search 0x553070 -> 0x559140 (`tradeAdmits` /
  `_trade_admits`, `_trade_admit_rows`). A route's path (its start 0x555380,
  its yields 0x54bdb0 and the path term 0x54e160, GetTradeRoutePath
  0x12ee30): the edge origin -> destination's path, else 0x5526a0: the edge
  DESTINATION -> ORIGIN's path walked backwards (0x541ae0 with the vertices
  swapped), else the fresh search's (`tradePath` / `_trade_path`). The
  city-state's route choice values each candidate on that path and takes the
  first CanStartRoute admits (`minorRouteCandidate`, `_minor_route_candidate`);
  the trade AI's list (0x78f210) asks the pathfinder alone (`routeInRange`).
- CONFIRMED: runs/h1_duelz1124 Shenyang -> Bologna (578 -> 384), started t180
  on 578,577,576,620,619,618,617,616,659,658,613,569,524,480,435,...,384:
  the walk laid that path at t147 with China's Trader 2818050 idle in
  Shenyang and reaches Bologna no more from t170 (t179's update with the same
  Trader idle there finds none and keeps it); the engine's replay admits and
  lays the route on it (the import's "a route the engine's walk cannot lay"
  case). runs/c108_t225_20261108T115945Z: 853 of the 1,946 pairs the game
  admits read the exact reverse of the pair the other way (396 of the 531
  that differ from the fresh walk).
- OPEN: the import starts the graph from the record's running routes alone
  (their courses); the pairs a single-turn dump admits off older paths
  (c108: 18 -> 14, 18 -> 5:589831, 54:11 -> 18:16) need the records before it.

## C-95: a move order's path steps on from an attack's plot, its attack child by the order's flags, a non-attack order's destination, a melee blow on a civilian — READ (0x2720a0 at 0x272434..0x272544, 0x2715a0 at 0x2717cd / 0x271870..0x2718d7, 0x1385c0, 0x889e0, 0x2714b0, 0x206960 at 0x206a1f), both twins

`search`'s attack child and its leaf rule, `pathNodes`' destination,
`foreignOnLayer`, `groundOf`'s `fighterSeen`, `predictBlow`
(cpu/core/tactical.ts); GPU `_tac_search`'s `strike` and `lone`,
`_tac_move_to`'s destination mask, `_tac_predict_pool`'s `d_civ`
(gpu/core/sim_tactics.py).

- NO LEAF IN THE A*: the step refusal from an attack's plot (0x26e5cd) is
  the breadth-first searches' wrapper 0x26e570 alone (the planning's, the
  danger map's); a move order's path (the A* 0x7a630 over 0x26f330, its
  validity 0x2720a0) links on from any node it accepted, an attack's
  included.
- THE ATTACK CHILD (0x2720a0 at 0x272434..0x272544): a child whose node
  carries +0x51 & 0x34 (a city at war, a district at war, a unit at war:
  set by 0x271be0 on a plot the player sees now) is refused, but for a
  formation whose pathfinder +0x1f8 is set and the domain +0x1a0 is not air
  (1), where it passes: under the order's attack flag 0x10 the child that is
  the destination (+0xd8 / +0xdc, or none set); without 0x10, under 0x1000
  at a child's turn (+0x1dc) above 1 — there refused where the child holds a
  seen unit at war that fights (+0x51 bits 0x20 and 0x40), lies beside the
  search's start (0x889e0: the six neighbours with the map's wrap) and its
  parent is at the stacking limit (+0x51 bit 7). So a path without the
  attack flag passes a seen unit at war in a later turn, and none at all in
  its first.
- THE FINDER'S BYTES (the pool's init 0x2715a0): +0x1f8 the OR over the
  formation's members of 0x1385c0 (GetCombat, GetRangedCombat,
  GetBombardCombat or the religious strength above 0, and unit +0x18ba
  clear); +0x1a0 the domain: 0 a sea formation or one embarked, else 2 land,
  1 air, 4 the rest.
- THE DESTINATION (0x2714b0 under the order's flags): an order without the

- THE LIST: each unit stores the (plot, ring) list its last look walked
  (unit +0x1f40, size +0x1f50). 0x58f3f0(unit, plot, add): with add the new
  list is walked (0x58b1d0 at the unit's sight +0x1998, see-through features
  +0x1470, terrain +0x14d0), added to the visibility counts (0x58aa90 flag
  1), then the stored list is taken off (0x58aa90 flag 0) and the new one
  stored; without add the stored list alone is taken off and emptied.
- WHO LOOKS AGAIN: the placement and the step (0x586d40), the removal
  (0x586a90), and the setters of the sight (0x56ce90 on +0x1998), of the
  see-through features (0x5704d0, +0x1470) and terrain (0x570560, +0x14d0).
  Nothing else calls 0x58f3f0: a feature cleared or grown, a district placed
  or a city founded leaves every standing unit's list as it was, and the
  plots it sees are the counts that list holds.
- PORTED: the plots a unit sees standing are its stored look while it was
  taken from the plot it stands on with its sight and see-through; a step
  takes it anew after the step's reveal (a mover's look from the plot it
  left is its stored one); an upgrade's new unit takes its own; a unit put
  on a plot by any other write takes its look at the first ask that stores
  (the sight walks: `plotsSeenNow`, `othersSee`, `cityStateSight`), the
  meeting asks (`seatSeesPlot`) store none.
- CONFIRMED (aimem, one seed each):
  - runs/h1_duelz1128 t88: China's Government Plaza clears the Woods on
    11:13; the barbarian Swordsman 4456471 on 12:13 since t84 never records
    China's Archer 1048580 on 10:13 (its record ages 4 at t88 to 11 at
    t105). The engines' fresh sight saw it every turn: 15 knowledge.army
    misses t88-t105, none on the stored look (--from 80 --to 106).
  - runs/h1_duelz1127 t108: the barbarians' captured Settler on 15:12 since
    t78 never records China's Builder 1638400 on 13:10 (t108-t129 carried,
    t108 under aimem); none on the stored look (--from 74 --to 110).
- THE OLD ID AFTER AN UPGRADE (0xa49cb0, the new unit): every other player's
  record of the old id stays and ages out; none is re-keyed
  (runs/h1_duelz1128 t86 city-state 3's 655367 -> 1179650: players 0, 2 and

- A PLAYER'S RECORDS FORGOTTEN: 0x5ecc10(kb, player) empties every type

- OPEN: a destroyed player's records go from every knowledge base at its

## C-98: a lump of Science or Culture completes the item in hand — READ (0x4c8e60, 0x4c8ea0, 0x3938e0, 0x393670), both twins

(gpu/core/sim_economy.py), from a Great Person's lumps
(`activateGreatPerson` / `_gp_apply`: its Science, Mary Leakey's Science
per Artifact, a per-adjacent Science or Culture).

- THE RULE: a lump goes to the item in hand through 0x4c8e60 (techs) /
  0x3938e0 (civics): with nothing in hand the bank takes it; else
  0x4c8ea0 / 0x393670 add it to the item's progress. Where the sum passes
  the cost, the bank (the overflow the next turn's yield pays in,
  `techOverflow` / `civ_tech_ovf`) is SET to the excess. At or past the
  cost the progress setter completes the item at once
  (`completeResearchNow`), and the city-states' catch-up runs on that gain.
  Callers of 0x4c8e60 / 0x3938e0: GrantYield 0x468540, the harvest
  0x95fbf0, 0x93ec40, 0x536480, 0x1fc390, 0x1fce20.

  actions, and city-states 2, 3 and 4 then hold it at 291 (AI_Research.csv
  t117: 1 turn, city-state 4 RESEARCHING). Metal Casting is at 0 in record
  118 and at 129.21 in record 119 (71.26 banked + 57.95 Science), as the
  engine now has it.
- THE REPLAY'S MAJORS: a ResearchCompleted / CivicCompleted that the log

## C-108: every seat's Trader walks its route; a major's trade list and route value read the Free Cities' cities — READ (0x5f0280, 0x78f210, 0x5e9b20), both twins

`commitRoute` / `traderHome` (cpu/core/trade.ts), `knownTradeCities` /
`routeValueOver` (cpu/core/aiTrade.ts); GPU `_apply_route`, `_routes_home`,
`_seat_route_income`'s international leg, `_city_lux_plots`,
`_city_strat_plots` (gpu/core/sim_seats.py), `_city_improvement_count`
(gpu/core/sim_masks.py), `_known_trade_cands`, `_major_route_value`
(gpu/core/sim_minors.py), the Trader training gate (gpu/core/sim_economy.py).

- THE TRADER: a route is the Trader's unit operation (UNITOPERATION_MAKE_TRADE_ROUTE,
  UnitOperations.xml) for every player, a major's as a city-state's: the
  unit stays on its owner's list, walking the route (`Unit.routed`,
  `TradeRoute.trader`), dies with it at a plunder, comes home at the origin
  at its end or a cancel. No route spends its Trader and none hands a new
  one back. The training gate counts the free Traders and the routes (each
  the Trader walking it).
- THE MAJOR'S KNOWN CITIES: a major's lists (0x78f210) and its route value
  K (0x5e9b20) walk its knowledge base's city entries, which the look's city
  arm 0x5f0280 appends with no owner filter: the Free Cities' cities are
  known cities of a major's list, after the majors' (`cityHolders`). A route
  to a Free City is international: its origin yields are the international
  leg's, the destination's terms read on the Free Cities' row (its luxury,
  strategic and improvement counts, its research for the progress rows),

## C-99 / C-128: every technology gained starts an Upgrade Units tree, the civic event never fires; a tree's units after its tick; the Nearest City Search's resource test; the plot's unit list — READ (0x4cd4c0 -> 0x800c60, 0x5bbf80 -> 0x27a180, 0x3a1ac0, 0x7cb3d0 -> 0x7d2190, 0x7eba40 -> 0x510d30, 0x74f40 / 0x763b0), the trigger both twins

`minorTechGained` (cpu/core/minorBuild.ts), run from `minorResearchBank`'s
completion and from `minorCompleteNow`; GPU `_minor_research_bank` and
`_minor_complete_now` (gpu/core/sim_minors.py) through `_mops_upgrade_start`.

- THE TRIGGER: SetTech (0x4cd4c0) raises AI_EVENT_GAIN_TECH on player
  signal +0x2b8 (0x4cd7a5..0x4cd7b5) for every technology it sets, the
  bank's completion and a boost's alike; the trigger handler 0x800c60
  (bound by 0x8007a0 at 0x800a33) makes the row's tree at that moment.
  runs/h1_duelp1128 t127 city-state 3: Banking boosted complete by Guilds
  with no research completing, the game's tree 5111814 holding Warriors
  1900551 / 1835016 (ours the same id and units). Over the five duelp
  duels a city-state's new trees each turn equal its technologies gained
  (AI_Research.csv's OWNED count) but on 5 turns with two technologies
  and one tree at the log and 2 with one and none (a tree ended before the
  log), none with a tree and no technology.
- THE CIVIC: the AI events' ids are the AiEvents rows found by the hash of
  their names (0x8c4af0 -> 0xcd1390, a table CRC over the bytes as they
  stand, case kept) through 0x27a180 (a binary search on the rows' hash,
  -1 none). The DLL names the civic event "AI_EVENT_GAIN_civic" (0x5bc4dd,
  stored @0xf2e084), a name no row holds (Leaders.xml: AI_EVENT_GAIN_CIVIC),
  so the id is -1; SetCivic (0x3a1ac0) raises it (0x3a1d85) and 0x800c60
  returns on -1 (0x800c7d). TRIGGER_CIVIC_UPGRADE never fires.
- A TREE'S UNITS AFTER ITS TICK (0x7cb3d0 at 0x7cb722): a tree not marked
  for destroy (+0x368) that is not temporary (+0x308), or whose root status
  (0x7cb7c0, +0x230[0]) is RUNNING (2) or FRESH (0), runs 0x7d2190 over its
  units (0x6092c0 on +0x488) whose turn is not done (+0x530): with
  m_allowRecruiting (+0x3c8) and no operation (+0x888 -1) each is released
  (+0x778 -1 through 0x1e60f0), else its turn is done (0x570b40). An Upgrade
  Units tree is temporary: ending SUCCESS or FAILURE it runs none. Move
  Unit's execution gives turn done only to a unit off its target (0x7eef38);
  the swap's Start (0x972a50) leaves its partner's job as it is.
- THE NEAREST CITY SEARCH's resource test (0x7eba40 at 0x7ebed5..0x7ebf03):
  an upgrade (0x5909a0) asking a StrategicResource (Units +0x2c8, its index
  +0x14) skips each city where 0x510d30 fails: the owner's CivilizationLevel
  row (0x467f20) with IgnoresUnitStrategicResourceRequirements (+0x29 bit 1,
  CIVILIZATION_LEVEL_CITY_STATE's true), else its stock less reservations
  (0x4aa790 ownership 0, r9b 1) plus ownership 1 at least
  STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_MINIMUM_FOR_UNIT_UPGRADING (GlobalParameters +0x690,
  1). A city-state always passes: `upgradeTarget` reads none.
- THE PLOT'S UNIT LIST (0x75c50, per layer): a vector of unit ids;
  placement (0x586d40 -> 0x750e0 -> 0x74f40) appends a unit not listed
  (0x76ae0), removal (0x586a90 / 0x586d40 -> 0x763b0) erases it keeping the
  rest in order (0x76a10), a layer change (0x75280) removes then appends:
  the list is the units' arrival order. Not ported: the recordings list
  units by player (h1_dump_ig.lua's `Players[p]:GetUnits():Members()`), not

## C-116: the lay-back leaves one slot empty, and a slot-count rebuild grants the free change — READ

Player_Culture.cpp, the slot rebuild's tail (dll_readings "C-94: the slot
rebuild").

- The lay-back (0x391650 at 0x391eb4..0x391f45): the new slots walked in
  order; before each, 0x3996b0 counts the empty slots (+0x430 / +0x440,
  policy -1) and the walk ENDS once one or none is empty; else 0x398cf0 takes
  the first saved entry of the slot's type, and a card 0x3930a0 admits is
  written with no ADDED signal (lapsed), a refused one spent. So a rebuild
  always leaves one slot empty. Engines: `carryLayout` / `_carry_policies`
  (the `placed` count).
- The slot-count change 0x3a2e30 (a slot type added to +0x4b8, or +0x528):
  save, clear (0x3942d0: one REMOVED signal per card the OLD slots held),
  build and lay back (0x391650), then SetCivicCompletedThisTurn(true)
  (0x3a1f20): the free policy change, which the AI spends at once — its
  SetSlotPolicy signals follow the clear's run.
- The importer (`slottedAfterRebuild`): the clear's run of signals is at most
  the old slots' count; the cards signalled after it were slotted anew and
  pay, the rest stand lapsed.
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelp1121 t203 (record t204): Triangular Trade replaces
  Liberalism at the turn's start, Big Ben (79087) rebuilds 7 -> 8 slots, seven
  REMOVED (Logistics .. Merchant Confederation), seven laid back, Liberalism
  signalled into the eighth: Xi'an / Shanghai civics amenity 2 -> 1 (Civil
  Prestige lapsed, Liberalism paying), Taiyuan 1; 1117 t235 the same shape
  (Expropriation replaces Rationalism, ten cleared, Rationalism into the
  eleventh).
- Open: the engines do not run the slot-count rebuild (a wonder's, Adam
  Smith's, a congress slot) — the free change it grants lands in the middle
  of the player's city walk, after the civics step where the replay applies
  the recorded layout.

## C-112: the full re-place keeps the forced citizens — READ (0x196440, 0x1956b0, 0x197230), both twins

`replaceAllCitizens`, `toggleCitizen` and `forcedPlots` (cpu/core/citizens.ts),

`lockTiles` arm (cpu/core/phase.ts), `setTileOwner` (cpu/core/seats.ts); GPU
`_place_citizens(full=True)`, `_toggle_citizen` and `_forced_plots`
(gpu/core/sim_minors.py), `_apply_citizens` (gpu/core/sim_seats.py),
`tile_forced`, `city_spec_forced`.

- THE CITIZENS OBJECT keeps two counts per hexspace plot (indexed by 0x5ce10
  in the DLL's 37-plot order): the workers +0x08 (count +0x18) and the FORCED
  ones +0x20 (count +0x30). A district plot's forced count is its forced
  specialists; the engines keep a plot's as `Tile.forced`, a district's per
  type as `City.specialistForced`.
- THE UNASSIGN (0x196440, the full reassign's first step) keeps the forced
  citizens: the unassigned count +0x68 is the population (City +0x588) less
  every forced count; a forced count above the plot's capacity (0x195940: 0
  on the centre and where the plot is not the city's, a district's specialist
  slots, 0 where no yield is above 0, else 1) is cut to it; while +0x68 is
  below 0 the forced counts are cut in hexspace order, index 0 up ("Removing
  forced workers to match city population went wrong" asserts +0x68 = 0
  after); then every plot's workers are cleared. The placement 0x197230 gives
  a plot as many entries as its capacity less its workers plus forced
  (0x19749f..0x1974a7) and less its forced count again (0x19750e..0x197523,
  the same 0x5ce10 index), so the unassigned are placed beside the forced and
  a district with k forced specialists offers its slots less 2k.
- THE TOGGLE (0x1956b0, the city command's plot arm): the budget is the
  population less the forced counts of the city's other hexspace plots;
  nothing while it is 0 or less; less the plot's own, one more is forced on
  the plot while the budget stays above 0 and the count is below the plot's
  capacity, else the plot's forced count is set 0; then the full reassign
  (0x19587d). The engines' `lockTiles` is this click on the plot's own city;
  `specialists` sets a district type's forced count, the re-place cutting it
  to the slots and the citizens.
- A PLOT CHANGING CITY: the losing city's capacity on it is 0 (0x195940's
  owning-city test at 0x1959a8) and AnnexPlot's reassign of the losing city
  (0x1a903c) cuts its forced count; the gaining city's vector holds none for
  it. `setTileOwner` drops `Tile.forced` on any change of city.
- Open: the lab records no forced count, so no recorded case confirms the
  population cut's order or the toggle's budget.

Unit operations (vtables at 0xd98ef8 FORTIFY, 0xd99548 HEAL, 0xd97970 the

  0xd3a6f7e8). CanStart 0x95e970: a formation, then (an AI's unit) 0x56ef30
  — a combat, ranged or bombard strength and domain 2 or 3 (land) — not

  the max); its update 0x9606f0 ends it at no damage (ACTIVITY_AWAKE). The

## C-102: the citizen pressure's falloff and the per-citizen term — READ; Stamford Raffles' city

- THE FALLOFF (0x1a1640, after the dominance raise): d = GetPlotDistance
  (0x1deb0) from the city's centre (+0x158 / +0x15c) to the plot, << 8; R =
  CITIZEN_IDENTITY_PRESSURE_RADIUS_CUTOFF (gp +0xf0, 10) << 8. d > R or R = 0:
  the city presses 0. Else w = (R − d) / R by the fixed divide 0x16e940
  ((a << 8) / b, truncated): floor(256 · (10 − d) / 10); the pressure ×= w by
  fx_mul_assign 0x16eb20 ((a · b) >> 8), kept where above 0. A city at 10
  presses 0, so the walk's reach is 9 (`LOYALTY_RANGE`).
- THE PRESSURE BEFORE IT: (population +0x588 + Great Works × +0x1aec) << 8,
  × the per-citizen term (0x16e7d0, (a · b) >> 8); where the owner dominates
  the plot's owner, × (100 + gp +0xec) << 8, divided by 25600 toward zero
  (the magic 0xa3d70a3d70a3d70b, sar 14). Per-citizen terms are halves, so
  the engines' order (`citizenPressure`: the raised term, then the citizens,
  then the weight, each product floored) reads the same 256ths.
- THE PER-CITIZEN TERM 0x1a1370: the player's 0x381040 (on player +0x1390):
  CITIZEN_IDENTITY_PRESSURE_BASE (gp +0xe4) << 8, plus the capital's +0x3068
  while a capital stands, plus the player property 0xdee04aee read through
  LOYALTY_FROM_EXCESS_SCORE_MULTIPLIER (gp +0x46c, 0.0 in Expansion2, so 0
  here). 0x1a1370 takes the capital's +0x3068 back off and adds the city's own
  +0x5f0 (while a capital stands); + CITIZEN_IDENTITY_PRESSURE_CAPITAL (gp
  +0xe8) << 8 in the capital (+0x5e8); + the head of the build queue's
  Projects_XP1 IdentityPerCitizenChange (0x179650 on +0x2170 -> the project
  row's +0x1c -> 0x28a940, a float cut to 256ths): PROJECT_BREAD_AND_CIRCUSES
  and PROJECT_WATER_BREAD_AND_CIRCUSES 1.0. The engines carry no Bread and
  Circuses project.
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelp1128 Guangzhou t240-245 reads 10.859375,
  −4.296875, −1.953125, −2.34375 as recorded (`citizenPressure`,
  `pressureTerm`); across the five duelp recordings every loyalty failure is
  another check's (the amenities, a starving city's −4 on its Food, a
  neighbour's growth) or the Raffles city below.
- STAMFORD RAFFLES (GREATPERSON_CITY_STATE_ABSORB_EXPANSIONS, Babylon
  Expansion2: MODIFIER_UNIT_ABSORB_CITY_STATE_AS_GIFT_AND_APPLY_MODIFIER with
  MODIFIER_SINGLE_CITY_ADJUST_IDENTITY_PER_TURN 10): the +10 lands on the
  absorbed city. The importer lays a person's city channel on its player's
  city holding the person's plot when the person absorbs a city-state
  (`importPeople`): runs/h1_duelp1127 Raffles spent on 7:12 t213, Mexico
  City's "Other" 12 from t214, Xi'an without it.
- Open: the +0x3068 / +0x5f0 writers (EFFECT_ADJUST_CITY_IDENTITY_PRESSURE,
  _FROM_AGES, _PER_CITIZEN): which carries the age's ±0.5 and the nuclear
  emergency's −1 (the engines cut the citizens, `emergencyPressureCut`); no
  duelp case.

## C-102 / C-99: the plot's unit list as an arrival stamp, the best defender's tie and Garrison City's standing unit — READ (0x75c50, 0x74f40 / 0x763b0 / 0x75280, 0x208b80 / 0x523d60, 0x810fd7..0x81101b), both twins

`arrive` / `arriveAll` / `arrivalOrder` / `plotUnits` / `bestDefender`
(cpu/core/units.ts), `cityGarrisons`, `garrisonCS` / `districtDamageLoss`
(cpu/core/combat.ts), `AiView.plotFighters` (cpu/core/aiView.ts),
`garrisonExecute` (cpu/core/operations/assault.ts); GPU `_arrive`,
`_arrival_key`, `_best_defender` (gpu/core/sim_seats.py, through
`_occ_set` / `_occ_set_new`), `_garrison_cs`, `_district_damage_loss`,
`_city_garrisoned`, `_x_garrison` (gpu/core/sim_minorops.py); the importer
`advanceHistory` / `importTurn` (cpu/harness/import.ts).

- THE LIST AS A STAMP: the plot's list (0x75c50) is the units' arrival
  order (placement appends 0x74f40 -> 0x76ae0, removal erases in place
  0x763b0 -> 0x76a10, a layer change removes and appends 0x75280). The

  unit (a spawn, a capture's or a conversion's unit, an upgrade's); a unit
  whose stamp names another plot sorts after the stamped ones. The replay
  stamps the recorded actions as they land and each unit `syncUnits`
  moves, in the order of its first logged step.

  (UnitAddedToMap, UnitMoved, UnitTeleported) before the record gives its
  stamp, the row's number, where that row put it on the plot it stands
  on; a unit no row placed is the earliest (0). An upgrade logs its new
  unit's UnitAddedToMap (runs/h1_duelp1117 t24 524289, t90 786439).

  holder's military unit not embarked of the greatest Combat and formation
  strength, the earliest arrival on a tie; it is the garrison the centre's
  strength, the damaged district's waiver and REQUIREMENT_CITY_HAS_GARRISON_UNIT

  unit on the city, the first unit of the plot's list whose formation class

## C-109: war weariness per combat, the turn's decay and the percent — READ

Player_Diplomacy's ledger: 0x1fb680 per combat (from the combat log
0x20d280), 0x3d7270 per turn, 0x3d04a0 the writer (adds the delta, floors the
total at 0, logs Player_WarWeariness.csv: Player, FromPlayer, Delta, New Total,
Reason). Ported in `weariness.ts` (`warWearinessBattle`, `wwEraBase`,
`wwWarPercent`, `addWw`, `warWearinessTurn`) and `_ww_battle`, `_ww_era_base`,
`_ww_war_pct`, `_ww_add`, `_ww_decay`; the wiki's era tables deleted.

- WHO: both players FULL_CIV (0x469db0 at 0x1fb801 / 0x1fb823), so a combat
  with a city-state, a Free City or the barbarians scores no one.
- SIDES by the combat type ([+0x50]) and its subtype (0x213cd0): a unit's
  side is its owner, a district's (0x213c80) the district's owner, a plot
  target's the plot's owner; a district side has no unit ([+0] / [+8] null).
- LOC, per side, on the combat's plot ([+0x48], [+0x4c]): 0x20a220 is true
  where the plot's owner is the unit's owner or one it HasAllied (0x3da560);
  WAR_WEARINESS_PER_COMBAT_IN_ALLIED_LANDS 1 (gp +0x76c) then, else (and
  for a side with no unit) _IN_FOREIGN_LANDS 2 (+0x770); + _PER_UNIT_KILLED 3
  (+0x774) where its unit's damage reached its max HP (0x56e0d0); the
  attacker + _PER_WMD_LAUNCHED 10 (+0x778) for a WMD ([+0x5c] != -1).
- BASE: X = 0x3d1450(player, foe, the pair's war state 0x2a8460): the war
  state's DiplomaticActions row's WarmongerPercent (+0x34), 0 for EMERGENCY_WAR,
  SUZERAIN_WAR, DEFENSIVE_PACT and a pair at peace, capped by
  m_iMaxWarmongerPercent (+0x1a48). The attacker's base is
  WAR_WEARINESS_WARMONGER_BASE 16 (+0x780) + trunc(Eras[the GAME era
  (0x2c3660 +0x108)].WarmongerPoints (+0x30) x X / 100); the defender's
  16 - X (0x1fba5f..0x1fba6b), so in a war of 16% or more the defender
  scores nothing (the duelw ledgers' one "Getting Attacked" row each: 32,
  loc 2 x 16, a war of percent 0).
- PERCENT: pct = the side's m_iOverallWarWearinessMultiplier (+0x18c8) +
  the foe's m_iEnemyWarWearinessMultiplier (+0x1808) [+ its own
  m_iDomesticWarWearinessMultiplier (+0x1868) where loc read allied];
  nothing at pct <= -100; amount = trunc(loc x base x (100 + pct) / 100),
  logged only above 0. EFFECT_ADJUST_WAR_WEARINESS (0xbe2d40 reads Amount,
  Enemy / Domestic / Overall; 0xbe35b0 applies) ADDS the signed Amount to
  the chosen multiplier: Fascism's Overall +20 raises it, Propaganda's,
  Martial Law's, Trung Trac's and Joaquim Marques Lisboa's -25 cut it
  (`wwPct`: the government's and the cards' `PolicyEffects.wwPct`, the
  Great People's `gpPerm` channel).
- DECAY (0x3d7270, from 0x3d7020 at the player's DoTurn): from every opponent
  o the pair relation 0x2a8610 holds for, with W[o] > 0, the player sheds
  WAR_WEARINESS_DECAY_TURN_AT_WAR 50 (+0x75c, "At War Decay") while o's
  flag +0x728 is set and o is at war with it (0x2a92d0), else _AT_PEACE 200
  (+0x758, "At Peace Decay"); a turn of combat does not hold it back. A
  peace (0x3dbcb0) sheds 2000 on both sides ("We / They Made Peace").
- The war's kind for an import or a recorded declaration: DiplomacySummary.csv's
  "At War" row, its name 0x2a8480's (`loadWarKinds`, `WAR_NAMES`).
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelp1128 (Rome / China, China's Surprise war of t203,
  the game era Industrial: base 52): the 33 Attacking rows (Rome's city
  104, Galley on its own plot 52, China's units abroad 104, from t223 under
  Fascism 124 / 62) and every At War Decay; `seat.warWeariness` in the
  replay 34 / 34 pairs equal over t205-240 (0 / 12 before over t205-216).
  The duelw ledgers factor the same way (1118 China t240-247 78 / 39 =
  104 / 52 x 75%, China holding Trung Trac and no war-weariness card).
- OPEN: the Domestic multiplier's one row (Defense of the Motherland, a card
  the catalog lacks); m_iMaxWarmongerPercent's one writer
  (EFFECT_ADJUST_PLAYER_MAX_WARMONGER_PERCENT, Cyrus, not in the roster).

## C-111: a captured city keeps its completed districts' locked prices and no progress by type; a district's repair is its city's queue; a unit's pillage takes the district's dearest building first — READ (0x1e8880, 0x173f70 at 0x17480e, 0x967300 / 0x967740, 0x9633c0 -> 0x24af90 -> 0x193190), both twins

`transferCity`'s `keptDistricts` (cpu/core/phase.ts), `captureCityState` /
`captureCityStateFor` (cpu/core/combat.ts, the minor's `districts` with their
`cost`); `districtRepairSite`, `placeSeatDistrict`, `districtPlots`
(cpu/core/decideObsCities.ts), the Builder's REPAIR arm and `unitMask`;
`pillageTopBuilding` (cpu/core/disasters.ts) from `hostilePillage` and the
seat PILLAGE's `wreckDistrict` underfoot; the replay's pillage case. GPU
`_transfer_city`'s `old_dcost`, the minor capture's `city_dist_cost` from
`citystate_dist_cost` (gpu/core/sim_orders.py), `_district_own_site` (the
district mask and the build arm, gpu/core/sim_seats.py), `_q_push`'s district
share, `_seat_city_produce`'s repair branch (gpu/core/sim_phase.py), the
REPAIR arm and mask, `_pillage_held(unit=True)` (gpu/core/sim_economy.py)
from the seat PILLAGE, `_barb_pillage_here` and the minors' `_plunder`.

- THE CAPTURE (City_Manager 0x1e8880, every transfer: conquest, loyalty,
  trade, the Lua TransferCity): the new city is a fresh city, its queue's
  arrays (+0x218 / +0x230 / +0x248 / +0x260) empty. Each COMPLETED district of
  the old city (+0xb08 set, not the centre: 0x24c250) is recorded (x, y,
  type +0x218, complete, pillaged, the two damages, +0xaa8 the locked price,
  the fallout) and made again in the new city (0x1ad930), its price set
  through the +0xa50 watch (0x1e60f0), then its pillage (0x1af5b0), whose
  hook 0x17e770 sets the new city's +0x248 to trunc(price x 75 / 100) where
  pillaged: the engines' lazy share at the repair's queueing (`resumeItem`)
  on the kept price. An unfinished district is not made again.
- THE REPAIR (City_BuildQueue 0x173f70, the district CanProduce): 0x1ae340
  with the IsPillaged functor (0x1ae7a0 -> 0x1af9a0 -> 0x24c3a0) finds the
  city's pillaged district of the type; at a plot naming it (0x17480e) the
  item is taken past the placement tests (0x35f2d0), the one-per-city and
  the population limit (0x17436a); refused before that where the type is
  locked (0x4090b0), the plot is under fallout (0x1aefa0), flooded or
  occupied. The Builder's repair (Unit_Operations_Repair CanStart 0x967300,
  Start 0x967740) takes the plot's pillaged improvement (+0x44, +0x4d bit 0)
  only, so a district is repaired through the queue alone; its completion
  0x175140 sets it whole without the new district's grants.
- THE PILLAGE (Unit_Operations_Pillage 0x9633c0): an improvement on the plot
  is pillaged (0x362b30); else the district's chooser 0x24af90 names the
  first of strictly greater Cost (+0x24) among the city's unpillaged
  buildings there (nothing on an InternalOnly district, +0xe1 bit 4, or one
  with hit points, +0x58 / +0x5c), pillaged through 0x193190 whatever its
  Buildings_XP2 Pillage; only where none stands is the district itself
  pillaged (0x1af930). The plunder reads the plot's district either way
  (0x1fc390 -> 0x51a080).
- Confirmed (one-seed traces): runs/h1_duelp1121 t140-141 the barbarian
  Line Infantry 4128797 on Xi'an's Holy Site 7:15 takes the Shrine at t140
  and the district at t141 (DistrictPillaged t141), the Shrine queued on 26
  at t148; the replay's Pillage Improvement 8 / 8 on t134-149 (7 / 8 before),
  read.seat.maintDistricts 15 / 15.
- Open: the coastal raid's target (0x95ba10, unread: the engines pillage the
  district); an unfinished district's plot after a capture (the engines leave
  it paved; the DLL makes none again); a captured minor's unfinished
  districts (the engines carry them in the registry).

## C-105: the district discount's refresh at a district's placement and at a city's placement — READ (0x181700 at 0x181a97 / 0x181ac2, 0x36dc00 at 0x36dcc2 -> 0x1eae70 at 0x1eb312 -> 0x409800), both twins

The player's district prices are a cache (Player_Districts +0x1a8, one entry
per Districts row) that 0x409870 writes for one type and 0x409800 for every
type. Its writers:

- every type: SetTech (0x4cd7f1), SetCivic (0x3a1dbd), the game's start
  (0x4cc740) and a city's placement 0x1eae70 (0x1eb312), which Player_Cities'
  city add 0x36dc00 runs for every city a player receives: founded (0x36de50

  at 0x181a97, then 0x409870 for its type at 0x181ac2): `paveDistrictTile` /

player as a 'city' step, every type's count at the completed count standing.

- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1117 t186: Chengdu's Campus completes, then

## H-1: a great person's price and its draw's era — READ (0x2f1c50, 0x2f8f70 -> 0x93e9e0 -> 0x2f94d0), both twins

- THE PRICE 0x2f1c50 (game, class, person era r8): the person era's
  Eras.GreatPersonBaseCost (row +0x2c); where the game era (0x2c3660 →
  Game_Eras +0x108) is neither the game's start era (GetStartEra 0x215b20,
  row +0x14) nor the person's, the person's is the later (0x93e9e0), and the
  game era is not the last (0x93e8a0): d = the eras walked from the game era
  to the person's (0x93eaa0), and d times price += floor(d × price × 0x1e /
  100) (0x2f1e10..0x2f1e22); then the speed (0x5254d0, CostMultiplier / 100)
  and down to a multiple of gp +0x5b0 (PURCHASE_DIVISOR). The class argument
  is never read: every class scales. `gpCost` (rules `gpCostTable`
  [person era][game era], `_gp_cost`).
- THE REPLACEMENT 0x2f8f70 (after a grant 0x2f74b0): the draw 0x2f94d0
  starts at the later (0x93e9e0) of the game era (0x2f1ba0 → Game_Eras
  +0x108) and the leaving entry's era (+8), walking forward to the first era
  with candidates (0x2f4990, 0x93eaa0); the entry it writes {individual,
  class, era, price}. `ensureGpOffer(from)`, `_gp_ensure_offer(from_era)`.
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelp1117-1128 Game_GreatPeople.csv, 137
  replacements: 130 at the later of the game era and the leaving era, 2
  past it with that era spent (1124 t145 Alfred Nobel, Modern, after Charles
  Darwin with the Industrial scientists spent), 5 on an era's turnover
  turn drawn before it; 1128 t93 Thomas Aquinas Renaissance in the
  Renaissance game era, both majors Medieval. Every price: 1124 Nobel 425
  (drawn in the Industrial game era, (660 + 198) × 0.5 = 429 → 425), Mary
  Leakey 620 (t173, (960 + 288) × 0.5 = 624 → 620), every other one its era's
  online base (Imhotep 60 at the setup, the Ancient start era). runs/h1_duelp1128
  t220: China's 483 points recruit Erwin Schrödinger at 480.
- OPEN: the setup's draws 0x2f7c10 (the start era); the per-class points
  every major's store gains with no source the engines hold (China +100 a
  class at t180 on all five duelp games, +50 at 1124 t160 and 1128 t183)
  and the store a later grant leaves at that amount and the fraction (1128
  t220: 483 − 480 → 150, the record's).

## C-111 / C-108: a route the records carry walks home and ends there, a Great Person's granted unit raises the best strengths, a major's wonder contract cancelled — READ (0x552bc0, 0xbd8be0 -> 0x4c1a30, 0x5d7e00), both twins

- A ROUTE'S END (0x552bc0, ported as `tradeRouteMinDuration` /
  `tradeRouteExpiry`): a route ends where its Trader comes home with the
  turn at its start plus the term the game era gives at the check. Every
  Route Ended (Expired) row of the five duelq Game_TradeManager logs lands on
  a turn the records find its Trader on the origin centre, and each earlier
  home arrival falls short of the term. A route begun in turn S is first
  carried by record S + 1. The importer (`importTradeRoutes`,
  `routeWalkOfRecord`) gives a record's route its start S (the first record
  carrying it less one) and its walk: the Trader's plot of the course and
  its leg (in from the destination, or from a plot further along the
  course), so a route imported or taken by the replay from the record walks
  home and ends in the engines' expiry. The engines' rule is unchanged.
- Confirmed (one-seed traces): runs/h1_duelq1121 Shanghai -> Xi'an (Trader
  5767183, begun t182) ends at t213 with the Trader home on 12:9, Shanghai's
  city.yields 0 misses t212-214 (5 Food / 5 Production / 1 Science over
  before); Hunza -> Shanghai ends t212 and is re-sent t213 by the minor's
  pick; runs/h1_duelq1124 from t138: Cardiff -> Shenyang (S114) and Bologna
  -> Shanghai (S118) end at t143, Granada -> Shanghai (S118) at t141, each
  re-sent the next turn.
- A GREAT PERSON'S GRANTED UNIT (EFFECT_GRANT_UNIT_WITH_EXPERIENCE 0xbd8be0
  -> 0x4c1a30): the unit made raises the player's best melee (and ranged)
  trained to its Combat as made (`activateGreatPerson` ->
  `raiseBestTrained`; `_gp_unit_grants` -> `_raise_best_trained`).
  Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1121 t140 Yi Sun-sin's Ironclad, China's
  m_iMaxMeleeStrengthTrained 50 -> 70, Xi'an / Taiyuan / Shanghai defense
  80 / 72 / 70 (read.city.defense 0 misses t141-143 from t134); 1127 t202 an
  Ironclad 65 -> 70; 1117 t88 a Galley 25 -> 30; the grants below the best
  (1124 t179 Battleship, t207 Submarine, t230 Spec Ops; Warrior Monks) move

- A MAJOR'S WONDER CONTRACT CANCELLED (the in-hand check 0x5d7e00, from the
  city update 0x5ce680 in the player's AI turn 0x5c2650): CANCELLED is the
  contract's eligibility failing (vt +0x98: the city's threat for a

## C-107: the founding's annex, lifetime culture and the border reads of the duelp records — READ (0x1a9f10, 0x1a8a30, 0x1a7710, 0x3a1fb0), both twins

`foundCityAt` (cpu/core/game.ts), GPU `_found_city_at` (gpu/core/sim_seats.py,
`_row_starting_tiles` in sim_init.py); `countLifetimeCulture` /
`addCivicProgress` (cpu/core/economy.ts) at the turn's Culture, a boost
(`markBoost`), a lump (`researchLump`, `applyLumpYield`) and Kupe's
pre-settle Culture, GPU `_count_lifetime_culture` / `_add_civic_progress`
(gpu/core/sim_economy.py); the replay's `seat.lifetimeCulture` against
PlayerCulture m_xLifetimeCulture.

- THE FOUNDING'S ANNEX: cityPlacement 0x1eae70 calls 0x1a9f10 (0x1eb2a9),
  which runs AnnexPlots 0x1a8a30 with the count max(0, StartingTilesForCity
  0x1ab460) and its ring flag set: GetRingPlots 0x6b130 (radius 1) walks the
  ring through the functor 0xd15268 (slot 2 0x1aca80 -> 0x1a7710), which
  annexes (AnnexPlot 0x1a8b70) a plot unowned, or owned by the city's player
  with no district on it (GetDistrictType 0x810d0 == -1), decrementing the
  count with no floor; then one GetNextBuyablePlot picker (0x1ab1c0) per
  plot the count has left, each annexed; then the envoy annex 0x1abf40 for
  each player holding envoys there. An annex is no culture claim.
- A CITY-STATE (CITY_STATE StartingTilesForCity 5): its six unowned ring
  plots take the count to -1, no picker draw (48 of 48 at t2 on
  runs/h1_duelw1103-1118); the envoy annex's A (+0xc less 0x1ab460) is 1
  from the founding, so its E envoys annex E - 1 (`envoyTiles`' `- 1`).
- CONFIRMED: runs/h1_duelp1117 t194 Shenyang, founded on Xi'an's ground,
  takes Xi'an's five ring plots (a CityTileOwnershipChanged row of each
  city) and 826 by one picker over range 1 after "Choosing a City Name";
  the replay's founding pairs now hold every plot of 1117 t195, 1121 t247
  (Wuhan), 1124 t223 (Quxian), 1127 t213 (Wuhan), where the engines took
  only the unowned ring.
- LIFETIME CULTURE: the civic progress setter 0x3a1fb0 sets the progress no
  higher than the civic's cost (0x3a20d6..0x3a2108) and adds the new less
  the old (+0x988[civic]) to +0x1050 where positive (0x3a21ac..0x3a21c1):
  every gain counts, a boost's share on a civic not in hand included, the

## C-110 / C-99: the unit's activity and the Fortify order's refusal — READ

The unit's activity (+0x5f0, a type hash; the records' `UnitActivityChanged`
rows name each change) gates the Fortify order: its CanStart (0x95e970)
refuses HOLD, SLEEP, HEAL, SENTRY and INTERCEPT (0x8be70). Ported as
`Unit.activity` (none for AWAKE and OPERATION; `unit_activity`, ACT_HOLD /
ACT_SENTRY), statecompare `activity`.

- AN OPERATION'S START (0x55280, the operations manager): OPERATION
  (0x490cc8e1) where the unit has Movement left (0x56c690), else HOLD
  (0x47c048b). The run (0x52f50 at 0x5337a) sets AWAKE once the queue is
  empty. Ported: `operationStart` from the move order (`orderOnce`,
  `_tac_move_to`) and the Fortify order's own start (`fortifyOrder`,
  `_fortify_order`: HOLD with no Movement, SENTRY at the max, 0x95ea70).
- THE SKIP TURN operation: its execution 0x9687a0 sets HOLD; its CanStart
  0x9685d0 (an AI's unit: not INTERCEPT, +0x1b28 -1). The homeland's End
  Turn (0x70cba0, from the homeland's moves 0x709d80) builds it (0x9686d0)
  for each unit of its list whose turn is not done (+0x530) nor dead
  (+0x770). Ported: `skipTurn` / `endTurn` (cpu/core/units.ts,
  tactical.ts), `_skip_turn` (sim_tactics); the barbarians' explorers and
  pillagers, whose turns the engines' passes close, take it too
  (runs/h1_duelq1117-1128: 1,031 HL: Explore rows beside an HL: End Turn,
  176 Pillage Improvement turns OPERATION, AWAKE, HOLD, Skip Turn).
- A RANGED STRIKE leaves its unit HOLD (`hostileRangedStrike`,
  `_hostile_ranged_strike`): the duels' 369 barbarian ranged strikes of
  Attack Units each end OPERATION, AWAKE, HOLD; their melee blows AWAKE.
  The operation whose start sets it is unread.
- THE PLAYER'S END OF TURN (Player_Units' end of turn 0x4ef6d0 at
  0x4f02ce): a unit on HOLD is AWAKE (0x53e20 -> vt +0xc0) where its owner
  is human or its fortification (+0xd50) is 0; on HEAL, where it is an AI's,
  or a human's whose +0x590 is not -1 or that holds no damage; a barbarian's units
  (0x469ce0 at 0x4ef82e) are left as they are. Ported in `refreshUnits`
  and sim_step's rest (HOLD alone: the engines produce no HEAL).
- An upgrade's new unit carries the old one's activity (runs/h1_duelq1127
  t114: city-state 2's Musketman 1572870 made SENTRY, its t115 Heal
  refused, 0 at t116; 1128 t206 Bologna's Infantry 3342340 the same).
- The replay takes each unit's activity from the records' action log
  (`History.activities`, `foldActivities`), as it takes its fortification.
- A formation's host keeps its own fortification (`mergeFormation`,
  `_form_up`): runs/h1_duelq1121 t126 city-state 2's Musketman 1900545,
  two turns dug in on 9:5, forms a Corps and reads 2 at t127; 1117 t159
  China's Army 3145732 the same; no recorded formation resets it.
- Confirmed (duelq, the AI score on the game's memory): runs/h1_duelq1117
  t10 the barbarian Scout 262147, HOLD from its t9 Skip Turn, Fortify in
  place refused (0, as recorded); 1121 t34 the Archer 1835022 after its t33
  pillage; 1124 t125-132 the Crossbowman 5177363 after its ranged strikes;
  1128 t167 the Man-At-Arms 5177366 after two End Turns; 1121 t163-164
  city-state 4's Skirmisher 1638401, SENTRY at t162 then teleported to 0,
  its Heal refused.
- Open: a blow on a unit sets it AWAKE (UnitDamageChanged then AWAKE:
  runs/h1_duelq1124 t16-17 the barbarian Spearman 327684, SENTRY, struck,
  AWAKE), unported; HEAL, SLEEP and INTERCEPT never set by the engines.

## C-112: a citizen an event takes re-places the city's citizens — READ (0x1c79b0 -> 0x194fb0 -> 0x196320), both twins

  ChangeNumUnassigned (0x194fb0): a negative count runs the full reassign
  0x196320 at once, the forced citizens kept, every other placed again
  (0x197230). `loseCitizen` (cpu/core/disasters.ts) re-places a city-state's

  `_minor_replace_citizens` and `_place_citizens(full=True)`.

  (CityPopulationChanged after the heals), the record's t34 citizens on 535
  with 491 dropped and its surplus 7; the engines kept the last-placed plot
  off and grew on 5 until the city's own re-place a turn later.
- THE REPLAY'S ORDER (cpu/harness/replay.ts, no DLL reading): a centre the
  pair's landed battles struck heals at the turn's end on the hit points they
  left (the game's heal follows the barbarians' blows: 1127 t22 Mexico City
  struck for 10, whole at its t23 city update, no defensive cancel of its

  cities' rows lands after the start (1127 t47: Xi'an's pick, then China's
  envoy to Mexico City annexing 360 on the second picker draw); a major's

  place theirs (1117 t16: China's village citizen on Xi'an's 649).
- Open: whether the AI's start sends a token envoy before its cities or
  after them is read from the log, not from the DLL's player turn.

## C-95: the rampage strikes with the move's whole list; its defender is one the barbarians see — READ (0x778b40, 0x771670, 0x208b80, 0x20a2a0), both twins

`rampage`, `strike`, `defenderAt` (cpu/core/tactical.ts); `_tac_rampage`
(gpu/core/sim_tactics.py).

- THE LIST: Barbarian Rampage (0x778b40) appends each unit it gives a
  target to the tactical object's unit list +0x270 (0x778dd0..0x778e63,
  0x30 each) and calls the strike 0x771670 on that target; the list is
  emptied only by the dispatcher 0x770ce0 (+0x280 = 0 at 0x770d30) as each
  move opens. The strike walks the whole list in its order, each unit with
  Movement left (0x56c690, +0xdb0 > 0): the units given a target before it

  joins nothing.

  its head (0x208b80, then the COMBAT_DISTRICT type test at 0x7716f4).

  strikes (0x964a40), its moves ended (0x56d6f0) and listed done (0x77d180).
  Melee loop: every other unit with Movement (each ranged one too where no
  fighter holds the target) MOVE_TO the plot with flag 0x10, its moves
  ended (0x56d6f0 at 0x771e67) and its id added to the done list +0x258
  (0x771e76..0x771ef5). A ranged unit that neither moved nor struck stays

  the plot (0x20a2a0 at 0x208cc0: its visibility count +0x290 and the
  unit's stealth; flag 0x100 skips it). The strike passes flags 0, no

## C-114: the great person claim on a points change and the recruit — READ

- THE TRIGGER: a class's stored points change only through SetPoints 0x43e050
  (ChangePoints 0x43b1c0 adds a delta, the total clamped at 0); a new value
  signals the game (signal +0x798, its handler 0x2f8100, connected by
  0x2f9750). The free points (+0x2c8, `Seat.gppFree`) are their own store and
  signal nothing: the World's Fair's 100 claim nobody until a class's points
  move.
- THE CLAIM 0x2f8100 (player, class): of every player who may claim the
  class's standing person (0x2f1e70: on the timeline, CanRecruitPerson
  0x2f28a0 = earnable and floor(points 0x43ce10, the free ones included) >=
  the price 0x2f72f0, nobody marked at entry +0x10), the one holding the most
  points (strictly more, the first on a tie); the claim 0x2f2e90 only when it
  is the player whose points moved. 0x2f2e90 marks the entry, notifies, and
  for an AI player recruits at once (RecruitPerson 0x2f8890: the grant
  0x2f74b0 with its replacement's draw, then ChangePoints by minus the price
  plus the refund 0x43ce00's percent, one change). That change signals the
  claim again only where it moved the stored points (`advanceGreatPeople`,
  `gpClaimable`, `gpClaimant`, `_advance_great_people`, `_gp_claimable`,
  `_gp_claimant`, `_gp_spend`).
- THE RECRUIT: a person whose class's points did not move is claimed by the
  player's own RECRUIT_GREAT_PERSON (the AI's leads its Gold patronage,
  0x6898b0): a seat verb, `SeatActionRecord.gpRecruit` (`recruitClaimable`,
  `_gp_recruit`); the action replay imposes the recorded grant
  (`completeRecruit`).
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1128 t181 the World's Fair's 100 free points:
  James of St. George (Engineer, 14 own) and Dimitrie Cantemir (Musician,
  163 own) claimed at the turn's points; Gaius Duilius and Colaeus (30 each,
  neither class earning) by the AI's recruit, Duilius at t181 and Colaeus at
  t182 (duelw1128 both at t181); 1117 t181 Trung Trac, 1121 t181 Imhotep,

## C-125: the planning's blow back where both blows would kill — READ, ported

The planning's combat simulation (0x791470) runs the game's own combat
result on the units as they stand: the forward blow at the target's plot and,
per spot, the blow back with the sides swapped (0x213e00 side 0 the target,
side 1 the unit) and the combat's location the spot (+0x48, 0x7918b0). A
melee blow resolves through 0x205720 -> 0x205f70 -> 0x206960, whose result
already holds the mutual-kill rule (0x206c34..0x206d62): where the
defender's total (its damage + the blow) and the attacker's (its damage + the
counter) both reach COMBAT_MAX_HIT_POINTS, the side whose total overshoots
further falls and the other is left at max - 1 damage, the attacker on a tie
(`jle` at 0x206d04). The result words the planning reads are the clamped
ones: +0xc4 (the defender's damage, the spot's +0x94 blow back taken) and
+0x7c (the attacker's, +0xac). A ranged result (0x207a80) has no counter and
no clamp; its +0xc4 is the raw damage.

- Ported: `predictBlow` (cpu/core/tactical.ts) and `_tac_predict`
  (gpu/core/sim_tactics.py) clamp a melee prediction where both blows would
  kill: dealt = the defender's health - 1 where the attacker overshoots
  further, else taken = the attacker's health - 1. The forward blow and the
  blow back share it, so a clamped forward blow is no kill (+0xc4 >= health
  false).
- Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1128 t50, the barbarian Archer 2752535 (77 damage)
  on 17:13 with player 1's Warrior 589828 (86 damage) on 15:11 among Attack
  Units' targets: the Warrior's blow back on 17:10 is 31 against the Archer's
  23 health, its counter 29; both would fall, the Warrior 15 over to the
  Archer's 8, so the Archer is left at 1 (22 taken) and the spot passes the
  survival filter (0x7767cb); the GAP gives the Archer 17:10 at turn 3 (Move
  17 10 Attack -9999), as logged; barb.move.family t50 equal.
- Open: the same Archer's walk to 17:10 ends on 17:12, the game's on 17:11
  (the move order's path); 1128 t30 Warrior 2031630's Move-only claim on
  14:13 for player 1's Warrior 524291 (68 health, Discipline): the forward 28
  / 32 and the blow back 32 / 28 put the spot under the exchange filter
  (64 > 56), the real t31 blow there 22 against 18 (CombatLog +2 / -2): no
  mutual kill, the input that keeps the spot unread.

  +0x20 0xbb93d0 the attach, 0x3a2e30 (slot appended, save, clear all,

  engines take each seat's slots before the transfer and after: the loser,

  trait attaches at the game's start, under no government, so nothing
  rebuilds then; every government after is built with the replacement

## H-4: the step's item multiplier in 24.8 and a Builder's wonder charge through it; the resources step after the economy; an event's pillage and a district's resource re-rank the luxuries — READ, both twins

- THE ITEM MULTIPLIER (City_BuildQueue 0x16f050 -> the order's step;
  0x183db0 for a building or a wonder): the step's argument holds the amount
  (+0) and the multiplier (+8), both raw 24.8. Each factor is turned into
  24.8 on its own — a float32 percent x 0.01 + 1.0, floor << 8 | trunc(frac
  x 256), so 1.1 is 281 / 256 — and multiplied in through fx_mul_assign
  (0x16eb20, (a b) >> 8); the player's additive percents are one factor; the
  amount is multiplied by the result (0x16eb20 at 0x18439d) and added to the
  item's progress (0xac650). Ported: `stepMultiplier` / `stepAmount` /
  `fxFactor` (cpu/core/production.ts), `_step_mult` / `_step_amount` /
  `_fx_factor` (gpu/core/sim_phase.py), the seat walk's step and
  `_seat_city_produce` reading them; the engines' factors run in one order,
  the item classes they key on disjoint.
- A BUILDER'S WONDER CHARGE (The First Emperor) is a step through the same
  multiplier: the charge (15% of the wonder's cost) plus the overflow store
  times the item multiplier (`wonderChargeBoost`; the GPU's charge arm in
  sim_orders.py). Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1121 t38, Xi'an's Pyramids at
  18.66 takes 16.5 x 281/256 = 18.109 (36.77 of 110, record t39).
- THE RESOURCES STEP AFTER THE ECONOMY (DoTurn 0x4e4560: 0x4c9640, 0x4e08f0,
  0x396860, 0x4967f0 ahead of 0x4a8ed0 at 0x4e46c0): the luxury rebuild
  (0x4a6110) and the parks (0x32deb0) run after the science, gold, culture
  (its civics, government and cards) and faith (its spread), so the ranking
  reads the amenities the economy left. Ported: `rebuildLuxuries` /
  `refreshParkAmenities` after `questReligion` in `seatPhase`;
  `_rebuild_luxuries` / `_refresh_park_amenities` after `_quest_religion` in
  the GPU seat turn. Confirmed: runs/h1_duelq1124 t91, China's change to
  Oligarchy (GovernmentChanged 23843, cards 11 / 36 / 24) takes Xi'an's
  civics amenities 2 -> 0 and the rank Xi'an 1 -> 3, Beijing and Chengdu
  3 -> 2 (record t92's luxAlloc); seat gold, culture and science t93-98, the
  culture's plot (6,10) at t92.
- AN EVENT'S PILLAGE AND A DISTRICT'S RESOURCE: an improvement newly
  pillaged or destroyed by an event (`scorch`, `destroyImprovement`, the
  drought's `droughtTile`, the coastal flood's `floodLowland`,
  `submergeTile`, a detonation, a sack) and a district or wonder placed on a
  bonus or luxury resource (`paveGround`, the district handler's 0x4ab4d0 as
  a centre's) change the owner's extraction (0x4ab4d0), its allocation (and a
  city-state's suzerain's) ranked anew (`extractionChanged`;
  `_extraction_changed_pairs` in `_scorch`, `_destroy_improvement`,
  `_drought_tile`, the sea rise, `_submerge`, the sack, `_detonate`,
  `_pave_plot`).
- OPEN: a city's amenities as the game caches them between refreshes:
  runs/h1_duelq1117 t88 China's unit 2293771 garrisoned in Xi'an leaves the
  map at city-state 3's turn (UnitRemovedFromMap 23301, the city-state's

## C-95 / C-123: a move order's path passes a district of hit points out of sight and a unit of another map layer; a walk's step reads its own formation's riders; a raid's start zeroes the tribe's raid score — READ (0x586360 at 0x5866c9..0x58671f, 0x2720a0 at 0x272618..0x272689, 0x816cb0 at 0x8177cf..0x8177e9, 0x149980 at 0x149b01, 0x7c7330, 0x152c00, 0x154b80), both twins

`groundOf`'s `pass` (`fortUnseen`, the layered `foesSeen`), `enterable`'s
`forts` (cpu/core/tactical.ts); `stepRefusal` / `stepUnit`'s `formed`
(cpu/core/units.ts); `barbOpStart` (cpu/core/barbarianOps.ts); the replay's
copy (`barbarianAi`, cpu/harness/replay.ts). GPU `_tac_enter`'s `rel` /
`forts`, `_tac_search`'s `fort_u`, `_tac_move_to`'s `formedB`
(gpu/core/sim_tactics.py); `_step_verb` / `_escort_rider`'s `formed`
(gpu/core/sim_seats.py); `_barb_start_op` (gpu/core/sim_barbops.py).

- A DISTRICT OF HIT POINTS OUT OF SIGHT: the path node's location bit
  (+0x50 bit 0x40) is 0x586900 under flag 1, each member's 0x586360. Its
  district test (0x5866c9..0x58671f), on a plot of another player at war
  holding a district of hit points (the city centre, the Encampment),
  refuses a unit whose ranged or bombard strength tops its combat strength,
  and a unit that fights only without flag 1. The node's attack bits (+0x51
  & 0x34: a city, a district, a unit at war) are set by 0x271be0 on a plot
  the player sees now alone. So a move order's path takes such a plot the
  player does not see now as a plain node, at any turn. The destination is
  tested under flag 0 (0x2714b0), which refuses it: an order for a city out
  of sight still has no path.
- FLAG 1 OF THE PATH (0x2720a0 at 0x272618..0x272635): the parent's plot
  ([rbp+0x30] / +0x32 through the map's vt +0x80) against the search's start
  (+0x158 / +0x15c) — equal, valid; else under flag 1 a parent whose +0x51
  bit 0 is clear refuses the child. Operation Move sets 0x1001 where the
  node's Can Explore datum is false, and for the barbarians (0x469ce0)
  whatever it holds (0x816cb0 at 0x8177cf..0x8177e9). A plot the player
  never revealed is entered and never left; an unseen centre it revealed is
  the way through.
- A UNIT OF ANOTHER MAP LAYER: the hostile defender the location test reads
  (0x208b80) is of the mover's layer. A plot whose only units at war stand
  on another layer (a religious unit under a land unit's path) is a plain
  node: its stacking count (+0x54) is tested as any plot's, so the
  destination at its stacking limit ends the search with no path.
- A WALK'S RIDERS: a formation's walk steps the riders it set out with.
  Another formation's rider on a plot it passes neither stops the step (its
  Movement, its stacking) nor rides on; the walk's own rider passes a plot
  it may not end on, the walk stopping short of one.
- THE RAID SCORE: the tribe's score Barbarian Raid Check reads (0x7c7330 ->
  0x152c00: tribe +0x78 + +0x7c against the node's Score 10) grows 5 at each
  pillage of a unit of the tribe (0x154b80: the unit's owner the barbarians,
  its group +0x11d0 the tribe). The raid's start 0x149980 writes +0x78 = 0
  (0x149b01) once its operation stands; the tribe manager's functions
  write +0x7c in the tribe's copy 0x14c9e6 alone. Each raid counts its own
  pillages.
- THE REPLAY'S COPY: the record's pillages of the barbarians' turn land on
  the state before their AI's copy runs; the copy takes each back from its
  tribe's score with the plot (`barbPillaged`), and a raid the copy starts
  zeroes the state's score.

## C-95 / C-123: a zone of control out of sight is none in a path's cost; Attack Civilians past a withdrawn civilian; the capture step through a plot of its own; a withdrawal's plot — READ (0x5033a0 at 0x5033f9..0x503400, 0x773270 at 0x773383..0x77339c, 0x530650 at 0x5307a4..0x5307d3), both twins

`inEnemyZoc`'s `seen` (cpu/core/units.ts) from `groundOf`'s `zoc`,
`attackCivilians`' `taken`, `orderOnce`'s `capture` / `walk`'s `onto`,
`civiliansAlone` (cpu/core/tactical.ts); `retreatPlot` (cpu/core/combat.ts);
the Great People's `retreatsWhenCaptured` (cpu/data/units.ts). GPU
`_tac_zoc_path`'s `seen` from `_tac_search`, `_tac_attack_civilians`'
`stands`, `_tac_move_to`'s `through` (gpu/core/sim_tactics.py);
`_retreat_plot` (gpu/core/sim_seats.py).

- THE SIGHT TEST 0x5033a0 (visibility object, unit): the unit's plot
  (+0x220 / +0x224) indexes the player's visibility counts (+0x290 -> +0x10,
  an int16 a plot); a count of 0 or less answers false before any other test
  (0x5033f9..0x503400: `movsx ecx, word [rax + rdx*2]`, `jle`). Past it a
  hidden unit (+0x15f0) of another player answers by 0x503320. The zone of
  control 0x530f50 asks it of each exerting unit beside the plot entered
  (0x53128e), after the district arm: a unit at war on a plot the mover's
  player does not see now zones nothing, in the path's cost (0x26e920 through
  0x26f980) as in the planning's. A district at war zones whatever is seen.
  The walk's own test (0x26fe20 at 0x270800) runs on the plot the unit has
  entered, whose six neighbours it sees: a path that walked into a zone it
  did not see stops there with its Movement.
- ATTACK CIVILIANS' END OF A TARGET (0x773270): after each unit's order the
  target entry's unit handle (+0x10 through 0x8e9d0) is resolved, and the
  loop returns only where it names no unit or a dead one (+0x770,
  0x773383..0x77339c). A civilian that CanRetreatWhenCaptured is the same
  unit on another plot: the loop goes on, each unit after takes the move
  order for the entry's own plot ([entry + 4] / [entry + 8], where the first
  unit now stands: no path), a melee one's turn done, and each ranged one
  within its range of that plot takes the ranged order on it and is done.
  The row's "Available Units: N" counts them; none logs a row of its own.
- THE CAPTURE IS THE WALK'S STEP (0x26fe20 -> 0x212500): a move order onto a
  plot of civilians alone walks its whole path in one walk, the plot before
  the civilians' one held by a unit of its own or not.
- THE WITHDRAWAL'S PLOT (0x530650): each district of the victim's player is
  tested by the location test 0x586360 with r8d = r9d = 0 (0x5307a4..0x5307d3),
  which never refuses a plot for its owner's own units: a civilian withdraws
  onto a centre its player's civilian holds.
- THE INSTALL: Units.xml's CanRetreatWhenCaptured is true on every Great
  Person chassis (UNIT_GREAT_SCIENTIST, _ENGINEER, _MERCHANT, _PROPHET,
  _ARTIST, _WRITER, _MUSICIAN beside the General and the Admiral), the
  Archaeologist, the Naturalist and the Rock Band.

## C-125 / C-95: flanking and support count about the defender unit's own plot, no river edge read; MEDIUM by the plot's layer-0 list; a killed target's record; the camp strike's orders — READ (0x521530, 0x51c810 at 0x51cc1c..0x51cc56, 0x5228c0, 0x786d50, 0x776140 at 0x776333, 0x8e9d0, 0x772940 at 0x772d2f..0x772f78), FIT (the camp strike's path), both twins

## C-133 / C-95 / C-134: the kept path's searches inside a queue run; the Trader target, the defending district and Pillage's own plot; the safe plot's unit at war that fights — READ (0x272aa0 at 0x272af9..0x272c76, 0x26ef40 at 0x26f123..0x26f162, 0x26e3a0, 0x782d0, 0x783980 at 0x7842df..0x7842eb / 0x784aec..0x784b36, 0x24c2f0, 0x774380 at 0x774481..0x7744a9, 0x716b90 at 0x716d53..0x716da1), FIT (the planning list's seen unit at war), both twins

`orderOnce`, `orderRun`, `walk`'s `kept` (`KeptPath`), `tacticalTargets`,
`pillage`, `safePlot`'s `fighterOnLayer` (cpu/core/tactical.ts); GPU
`_tac_move_to`'s `order` / `under0`, `_tac_targets`, `_tac_pass`'s pillage,
`_tac_safe_plot`, `_tac_search`'s kept-out plots (gpu/core/sim_tactics.py);
`groundOf`'s `stand` (the fit).

- THE KEPT PATH INSIDE A RUN (0x272aa0, the kept-path flag +0x5d8 set by the
  queue run 0x52f50): each MoveTo execution asks the formation's path. With
  fewer than two kept nodes (the unit stands on the kept goal) the requested
  plot is searched unless it is the kept goal, which is no path. Else a goal
  node flagged out of sight (node +8 bit 1) whose plot the player sees now
  (the visibility count +0x290 above 0) is searched afresh
  (0x272af9..0x272b95); on no path the requested plot is searched unless it
  was that goal. Else the next node (count - 2) not flagged, the kept path
  is taken unsearched (0x272bd7). Else — the next node flagged — the kept
  path's last node of its first turn (0x782d0(path, 1)) is searched for
  (0x272c24); none such, or no path to it, the requested plot is searched
  (0x272c60), unless it was that node.
- EVERY SEARCH KEEPS ITS PATH (0x26ef40): after GeneratePath (0x7a630 at
  0x26f11e), found or not, the kept goal takes the plot searched (0x7eb220
  at 0x26f139), the kept path the finder's (0x778f0 at 0x26f157) and its
  flags are laid (0x26e3a0 at 0x26f162): walking from the start, the first
  node on a plot the player does not see takes bit 1, a goal not seen bit 1.
- THE TURN'S LAST NODE (0x782d0(path, T)): from the start toward the goal,
  the first node of turn T whose next node is of a later turn; the goal
  where its turn is T.
- THE ENGINES run the order again for the plot the rule names (`orderRun`'s
  `search`), a run for another plot than the order's searching the order's
  once it finds no path or stands on its plot; the walk asks the rule before
  each step after the search's own.
- THE TRADER TARGET (0x783980 at 0x784aec..0x784b36): a unit of the trade
  layer of another player, of formation class 2, with a route (0x58fc40), of
  a player at war (0x3dcec0), not immune to plunder on the plot's ground
  (0x58fc20 with 2 on land, 0 on water).
- THE DEFENDING DISTRICT (0x24c2f0; 0x783980 at 0x7842df..0x7842eb): a
  district ends its plot's chain (no unit, camp, hut, Trader, civilian or
  improvement entry) only where it defends — a city centre, or a district
  whose type has hit points, complete (+0xb08) and not pillaged (+0xc88).
- PILLAGE'S OWN PLOT (0x774380 at 0x774481..0x7744a9): a unit off the target
  on a plot whose district type (0x810d0) is not -1 takes no district
  target; one on a plot with an improvement (+0x44) no improvement target.
- THE SAFE PLOT'S UNIT AT WAR (0x716b90 at 0x716d53..0x716da1): the plot's
  units of the mover's layer (0x75c50 of 0x901e0) are tested by 0x5861f0,
  and the plot is left out only where its out-flag is set: a unit at war
  with a Combat, Ranged or Bombard strength (0x523520).
- FIT (the planning's list, 0x26d890): a formation with no fighter lists no
  plot it sees now that a unit at war of its layer holds, and lists one out
  of its sight whatever stands on it (the list's location test 0x586900
  under 9 unread for it).

## C-96: every player's build step drops a building CanConstruct refuses at the queue's head, the front check asking the next — READ (0x16f050 at 0x16f09a..0x16f180, 0x178250 -> 0x17f070 -> 0x17e8d0, 0x170450 at 0x17071d), both twins

`headLetGo` and `districtPillagedIn` (cpu/core/production.ts), run by the
majors' walk (`seatPhase`), a lump (`applyLumpYield`) and `freeCityBuild`;
`_head_let_go` (gpu/core/sim_phase.py), run by the walk, `_lump_step` and
`_free_city_build`. The city-states' pick shares `districtPillagedIn`
(`pickDistrictPillaged`).

- THE STEP'S HEAD CHECK (0x16f050 at 0x16f09a) is every player's: the
  caller (0x177d10) has read A toward the head the step starts on; a head of
  entry type 1 is asked CanConstruct (0x170450, last argument set). Its
  prerequisite-district test (0x17071d) runs before the held-building test
  (0x1707f1): the city's district of the building's PrereqDistrict (or its
  replacement, 0x408860) complete, 0x1ad720 (pillaged) clears the result
  (+0x2a), held building or not. A wonder with progress on a plot a hostile
  unit holds is refused at 0x170db8.
- A MULTI-ITEM QUEUE: the refused front is removed, not moved (0x17f630:
  the entries shift down one, the count falls), its progress kept by type
  (0x17f5a0); the queue process (0x178250, +0x3ac set) runs the front check
  0x17f070 on the new head, whose building arm (0x17e8d0) asks the same
  CanConstruct and pops again, the process re-running while an arm pops;
  then the step works the head with A, or with nothing queued adds B (the
  plain Production) to the overflow (0x16f62d), and 0x175c80 fires the
  empty-queue event. The unit / district / project arms (0x17f3a0, 0x17ed30,

## C-133 / C-95: the carried orders run in the unit list's order; a path comes ashore off water only by the disembark test — READ (0x7df30, 0x554e0, 0x523e0, 0x52e90, 0x54910, 0x2720a0 at 0x272380..0x27240d, 0x52fb90 at 0x52fb9d), both twins; UpdateOpenNode's walk and flag 2's plot — READ (0x79560, 0x2720a0 at 0x2721c3..0x27220d / 0x2724c8), unported

refusal (cpu/core/tactical.ts); GPU `_tac_with_short`, the entry's key at

- THE MANAGER'S VTABLE begins at 0xcff7c0 (the first slot 0x523a0): the
  queue's push 0x526a0 is its +0x60, the handler by operation type 0x53e80
  its +0x80, an operation's start 0x55280 its +0x130, the queue run 0x52f50
  its +0x138, the front operation's validity sweep 0x54910 its +0x150, the
  queue's turn 0x523e0 its +0x170.
- THE TURN'S DEACTIVATION (Player::Processor::DoAutomation 0x7df30, from
  DoTurnDeactivate 0x7eb60 at 0x7eba2): for a live player it walks the
  player's unit list (PlayerUnits +0x12e8 -> +0xd8, next +0x10: 0x7e06e,
  0x7e32a) and calls the manager's +0x50 (0x554e0) on every unit. 0x554e0:
  a unit alive (+0x770) with a pending operation (+0x2178, the front
  +0x2168) asks the front operation's handler (its vt +0x38); where it
  answers, the queue's turn 0x523e0 runs — for a unit in ACTIVITY_OPERATION
  (+0x5f0 = 0x490cc8e1) the queue run 0x52f50 (+0x138), the operation
  swept (+0x150) where the run is done —; where it does not and sets its
  flag, 0x52e90 empties the queue and clears the formation's kept path
  (0x265fd0). So the move orders a player's turn left short run again as
  its turn deactivates, in the unit list's order — the pool's slots
  ascending —, not in the order they were given; a formation's order at
  the least slot of its members (each member holds the operation).

- THE LOOK'S DISTRICT PLOTS (0x7877e0): a plot seen (visibility count above
  0, 0x7878e1) or only revealed (+0x2f0, 0x787c64) that holds a district of
  any kind (plot +0x10 not -1, an owner at +0x1c) takes 0x5f0280 with the
  district's handle — the city's centre is one such district, not a case
  apart; a plot with no district and a +0x1e not -1 takes 0x5f0490.
  0x5f0280 resolves the district (0x57b20), finds or appends its city's
  entry and fills it from that district (0x5efaf0): the city record
  (0x5ef9a0, where the entry's age is not 0), then, where the district has
  hit points (GetMaxDamage of 0x5e97d629 above 0: the City Centre, the
  Encampment), its own 0x20-byte entry by its handle: +0x14
  GetDefenseStrength with the garrison flag 0 (0x24ae80: the city's standing
  strength and the garrison term of the district's own plot), +0x18 the same
  where its own outer damage is below its most, +0x1c its strike
  (0x249ee0). So a known city holds an entry for its Encampment on a
  revealed plot, and 0x5eb2c0 (without its byte: the strongest of each
  entry's defense - 10 and walls) reads the Encampment's garrison.

- THE RALLY'S ADVANCE (0x73f0c0, called per team by the teams' update
  0x73f7d0 at 0x73fadb behind the team update 0x73fba0, where the
  operation's definition byte op +0x128 stands: AllowTargetUpdate, def
  +0x30 beside TargetType +0x28 and TargetParameter +0x2c): goal 0 (team
  +0xe8; goal 1 where it is none) against goal 1 (+0xf0), in axial columns
  (x - floor(y / 2), the x difference wrapped by the map's width) and rows.
  With v the step from the rally to the target and a . b = 3 (a.q + a.y /
  2)(b.q + b.y / 2) + 2.25 a.y b.y (single precision; constants 0.5, 3.0,
  2.25 at 0xd20458, 0xd26894, 0xd6df90): each live member (team +0x18) whose
  step back to the rally has a product p with v at or below 0, and whose
  step on to the target has a product whose product with p is not above 0,
  where p is below the least so far (from 0) sets the point (rally.q -
  trunc(v.q x p / (v . v)), rally.y - trunc(v.y x p / (v . v))), in double
  precision. The point's plot becomes goal 0 where it is on the map, not
  impassable (plot +0x3a bit 3) and unowned or the player's own — the
  player's own alone where the team definition's byte +0x10 stands
  (SafeRallyPoint, behind the two strength advantages +0x8 / +0xc). With a
  member of the sea domain (+0x650 0) and that plot not water, the ring walk
  0x6b000 (-> 0x6af80 -> 0x69010) within 3 of the target with the lambda
  0x740bd0 takes the first water plot. Only 0x73e7d0 (the start, Naval
  Choose Target, a settler's new plot) and 0x73e870 (the switch to the
  backup, whose value at op +0x380 holds the candidate's target +0x64 and
  rally +0x5c, 0x73e610) write goal 0 besides.

  barb.move.*).
- THE OPEN LIST (0x775a0, 0x79560) is a doubly linked list (+0xf0 head,
  +0xf8 tail, a node's +8 next, +0x10 previous), sorted by key (+0x18);
  within a key its nodes stand as the walks leave them. AddToOpen: an empty
  list takes the node; strictly below the head by (key, cost +0x1c) it goes
  first (0x77622..0x77632), strictly above the tail last
  (0x77646..0x77656); else, |key - head's| against |key - tail's|
  (0x774c0): nearer the tail the walk from the tail passes every node
  strictly above it and puts it after the first that is not
  (0x77710..0x7773f); else the walk from the head passes every node
  strictly below it and puts it before the first that is not
  (0x777d0..0x77823). UpdateOpenNode: a re-keyed node whose key is at or
  above its predecessor's stays (0x795c0); else it is unlinked and walks
  headward past every node of a greater key, no cost read, to stand after
  the first of a key at or below its own (0x795f0..0x795ff), at the head
  where none. So a re-keyed node stands after a turn-end node of its key
  (the turn-end node's cost is above its key), and the walks that follow
  stop on a key's nodes as they stand, not in their costs' order.
- Ported: TS keeps the list itself (`open` in list order, `addOpen`'s two
  walks, `reparent`'s headward walk, the head popped). The GPU keeps its
  sort key and adds a level between the key cost and the cost past it: a
  key cost's nodes stand as blocks — the nodes of the key cost alone that
  came by a re-key or after one, then the turn-end nodes after them, in
  their costs' order — and a block's index is the level. A re-keyed node
  takes the highest level of its key cost, one more where a turn-end node
  holds it (`rekey_level`); from the head a node of the key cost alone
  takes level 0, a turn-end node the lowest level holding a turn-end node
  at or above its cost, else the highest; from the tail a node takes the
  highest level holding a node at or below its cost (`place`). The level
  holds 0..3 (two bits of the key; the tie 16).
- Confirmed: the level order against the list itself, 60,000 random runs of
  inserts, re-keys and pops (keys of two to six values): every pop equal,
  no level past 3. The one-seed aimem traces hold every row of the base.
- THE EMBARKED STATE'S MOVEMENT CAP: the placement 0x586d40 picks the
  unit's state at 0x587042..0x5870aa — on a water plot, unless the plot is
  owned (vt +0x40) and its domain mask (+0x14, 0x81240) takes the unit's
  own domain (+0x650), a unit that can embark (0x56c480) and is not
  embarked takes UNIT_EMBARKED (0xfbb4f61); on any other plot an embarked
  unit takes 0x23c8f020 — and applies it at 0x58741c..0x587486: where the
  state differs from IsEmbarked (0x8be30), SetEmbarked 0x5706e0 (the
  tracked bool +0x658, its value +0x6b0, the event 0x84c1fdd6), then
  Rules::Placement's vt +0x68 (0x531ef0; the instance 0x533260, its vtable
  0xd503b0): the unit's Movement (+0xdb0) above its GetMaxMoves (0x56e130
  << 8) in the new state is taken off by ChangeMoves (0x56cc70). The walk's
  step 0x26fe20 prices the step first (0x270be0 / 0x270980 at
  0x270287 / 0x2702f1 off the formation's +0x218), places the members
  (0x587ca0 at 0x270444) and only then pays (0x265d80 at 0x270776: the
  formation's +0x218 and each member's ChangeMoves by the cost, floored at
  0). 0x270be0's chain keeps the disembark rule's excess (0x26ee90 into the
  context's +0x38) out of the cost it returns (+0x34 clamped by +0x2c /
  +0x30). So at every shore, owned water or not, embarking or landing: the
  Movement is capped at the new state's GetMaxMoves, then the step's cost
  is paid. The engines capped before the payment off owned water alone and
  after it at the other shores.
